title: The Distorted Mind and the Divine Number
english: The Church is the true knowledge of pure souls of ages and worlds and of the judgment and providence within them. The Preacher is Christ, the generator of this knowledge; or the Preacher is the one who, through ethical theorems, purifies souls and brings them to natural contemplation.

Regarding 'vanity of vanities' (Eccl 1:2), the Preacher says, 'vanity of vanities, all things are vanity.' To those entering the intelligible Church and marveling at the contemplation of the things that have come to be, the word says: do not think this is the ultimate end reserved for you by the promises; for all these things are vanity of vanities before the knowledge of God himself. Just as medicines are vain after the perfection of health, so the discourses of ages and worlds are vain after the knowledge of the Holy Trinity.

Regarding 'there is no remembrance of the former things' (Eccl 1:11): if there is no remembrance of the former things, how does David say, 'I remembered days of old' (Ps 76:6) and 'I remembered eternal years' (Ps 76:6)? Or will the total oblivion of all these things occur whenever the rational nature receives the Holy Trinity; for then God will be all in all (1 Cor 15:28). If the concepts of things occurring in the intellect lead the mind to a remembrance of things, the mind having beheld God is separated from all concepts; therefore, the mind receiving the Holy Trinity forgets all events.

Regarding 'God gave the sons of men a bad distraction' (Eccl 1:13): 'evil' refers to that which is superfluous, not that which is opposed to the good; for God gives nothing of that, for He is not the cause of evils, being a source of goodness, unless it is said He gives in the sense of forgiving according to the logic of abandonment.
Regarding 'being strayed, it will not be able to be adorned, and being lacking, it will not be able to be numbered' (Eccl 1:15).

Regarding the distorted, the impure mind, he says: 'for a distorted heart is made crooked by evil' (Prov 3:8). But he named wisdom as 'order' in the Proverbs, where he says: 'order is wisdom to youths' (Prov 3:21); 'therefore wisdom will not enter a craftily-evil soul' (Prov 12:10). Yet he did not say: it will not be able to be adorned, but: it will not be able to be adorned-upon; for life indeed adorns someone rightly, but the wisdom of God adorns-upon. Thus, indeed, a distorted mind is able to be adorned, but is not able to be adorned-upon, unless through the virtues it cleanses itself and makes itself a useful vessel to the Master.

The number of God, which counts the holy spirits as some kind and appointed order, declares: 'for of numbers, he says, multitudes of stars and names of good things for all of them' (Ps 147:4). By this number the Lord also commands Moses to count the sons of Israel (Num 1:2); but what does David say concerning the crawling men and those serving pleasures? 'There are crawlers of whom there is no number' (Ps 144:10); and in the Proverbs Solomon says concerning evil: 'for having wounded many, it has cast down, and they are countless whom it has slain' (Prov 10:25). What is therefore said here is a deficiency, and the slain and the crawlers are of the same state, which does not fit the spiritual number.

And if David says also that the wisdom of God is not a number, he writes not as if its worthiness were not of the number, but as if it were not of the nature to be subjected to number because of being incomprehensible. For just as the invisible is said in two ways, and that which is not of the nature to be seen, as God, and that which is of the nature to be seen, but not being seen, as iron in the depths because of being covered by water, so also the countless is said in two ways, and that which is not of the nature to be counted, and that which is not being counted because of some cause.
